condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

1. The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (MEMR) together with UNDP aunched the Sustainable Energy Fund (SEF) Grant for incentives for Rooftop Solar Power Plants (PLTS) as solar PV rooftop is one of the key-action in order to support the target of 23% RE portion in the national energy mix. There were 324 beneficiaries with a total incentive fund IDR 7,963,750,000. The program implementation can encourage: a. total 14,464 kWp generated capacity from the Solar PV Rooftop installation b. total IDR 38,464,027,230 RE investment from the Solar PV Rooftop Capex c. total 13,490 ton CO2e emission reduction (per year)
2. New collaborative highlights in 2022 include the partnership with the National Board of Zakat (BAZNAS) and Bank Jambi in co-financing the construction of the micro-hydro in Kerinci, Jambi. The local government has also provided an in-kind contribution for clearing the land status for the micro-hydro development (2). The project also co-shared with MEMR to conduct some of the MTRE3 projects. The MEMR covered the venue costs or provided in-kind contributions such as technical assistance during the meetings with stakeholders on energy efficiency and GHG inventory activities. The total in-kind from the government sector is USD 2,697,780 from the total target of USD 8,000,000.
3. In addition, UNDP also co-financed with Indonesia Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KADIN) and PT. SMI (a state-owned enterprise under the Ministry of Finance, specialising in infrastructure financing) to encourage renewable energy dan energy efficient projects, through equity investment. The total equity investment from the private sectors is USD 30,307,867 from the total target of USD 52,000,000
The NAMA proposal is expected to be implemented at provincial level, and will have a transformational impact for promoting investment in RE/EE sectors. Total numbers of Climate Mitigation Proposals being developed and registered to SRN are 7 (seven). It consists of 3 Renewable Energy Climate Mitigation Proposals and 4 Energy Conservation Climate Mitigation Proposals that are registered into SRN (National Registry System) managed by the Ministry of Environment and Forestry (MoEF/KLHK). 1 Climate Mitigation Project Proposal in Hydrogen with HDF Energy has succeeded to pass the 1st stage of GCF through National Focal Point (MoF).
Developing “ Single - Window service ” institutional guidelines for streamlining RE and EE investment permit system at Provincial level
This activity was carried out from the previous year (2021).
The development of the ‘RE/EE Investment Guideline and Recommendation’ has been completed and submitted to DJEBTKE – Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (MEMR/ESDM) (Attachment 124a,b,c,d). Dissemination to related local governments in 4 MTRE3’s pilot provinces (NTT, Jambi, Riau, West Sulawesi) has been conducted. The project will follow up with training on the guideline and RE/EE investment procedure to related local governments. The objective of the training is to enhance the capacity of local government in RE/EE Investment, specifically to DPMPTSP and ESDM, as they hold strategic roles in regional investment and are expected to function as the offline IMSC (Integrated Market Service Center).
Establishing “Integrated Market Service Center” to support sustainable investment in RE and EE
The document of ‘RE/EE Investment Guideline and Recommendation’ also provided recommendation for the enhancement of RE/EE investment information system by improving LINTAS-EBTKE website as a one-stop information center for RE/EE investment (Attachment 124e,f,g). The LINTAS-EBTKE enhancement has been done. LINTAS-EBTKE will contain all relevant information on the RE/EE investment process and procedure, including potential, business process, permitting system and public services. The connection between LINTAS-EBTKE in the central government and the local information system at the provincial level (4 provinces of MTRE3 as pilot project) is expected to support the full function of online IMSC.
A capacity building on the LINTAS-EBTKE operationalization for local governments in 4 pilot provinces was conducted on 29 September 2022 (Attachment 164a,b). Currently, the update process for the LINTAS-EBTKE content is in progress under DJEBTKE coordination. Further activity that will be conducted by the MTRE3 Project is the ‘new’ LINTAS-EBTKE’s launching.
2.1.1 Updating the RE/EE database information (specifically in 4 pilot provinces) and MTRE3’s product
The database for all MTRE3’s project activities is completing through the UNDP Indonesia’s sharepoints
.1.2 Disseminating the MTRE3’s product information to relevant stakeholders, including launching and promotion on SEF grant for Solar PV Rooftop Incentive
The MTRE3 project’s product information is finalizing. The product information of MTRE3 will describe 3 (three) main components with different focus.
Component 1: Translation of the national energy mitigation actions through the RE/EE Policies at local level
Component 2: RE/EE market transformation through: (1) facilitation of RE/EE projects, (2) encouraging the IMSC implementation, and (3) providing direct incentive for solar PV rooftop development
Component 3: Development of Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) for RE/EE projects, as well as supporting the carbon trading and carbon pricing system development
Some of MTRE3’s product information will be compiled in the form of a mini booklet (Attachment 146). The dissemination plan will be implemented through a webinar series activity during November 2022 - March 2023.
The launch of the SEF grant for Solar PV Incentive was held on 10 February 2022 (Attachment 147). MTRE3 Project, DJEBTKE ESDM, and BPDLH (IEF) promote the SEF grant for Solar PV Incentive regularly to public/potential beneficiaries by using related promotion media (Attachment 148). Some of the promotion activities to public include:
Promotion at the ‘BeritaSatu – Green Talk’ program in April 2022. (Attachment 149a)
Promotion at the ‘SDG’s Talk’ event conducted by UNDP Indonesia in March 2022. (Attachment 149b)
Periodic promotion to prospective beneficiaries, especially through EPCs and or related partners (Attachment 144)
Promotion through the testimony article at kompas.com (https://biz.kompas.com/read/2022/10/27/130627628/insentif-plts-atap-dorong-ebt-dan-pangkas-tagihan-listrik)
Promotion through the MRT station’s media
Promotion through related institutions (UNDP, ESDM, BPDLH) and beneficiary’s social media

2.2.1 Implementing of SEF Grant Incentive for Solar PV Rooftop
In order to cope with the SEF Batch-1 facility challenge, MEMR and MTRE3 project has designed the concept of Performance Based Payment (PBP) as a form of SEF batch 2 support scheme, especially for the Rooftop PV mini-grid project. Solar PV rooftop is one of the key-action in order to support the target of 23% RE portion in the national energy mix.
In order to support the implementation of SEF Grant Incentive for Solar PV Rooftop program, MTRE3 Project in collaboration with BPDLH (as the responsible party) to distribute a total incentive fund of IDR 23 billion to program’s beneficiaries. In addition, a ISURYA website has been developed to facilitate the applying process of SEF Grant Incentive for Solar PV Rooftop for the prospective beneficiaries (https://isurya.mtre3.id/ ).
After the launching of SEF Grant Incentive for Solar PV Rooftop (during April to November 2022), there were 8 (eight) verifications process that have been held to verify applicants of the Solar PV Rooftop incentive:
8-9 April 2022 (Attachment 150a)
13-14 May 2022 (Attachment 150b)
17-19 June 2022 (Attachment 150c)
22-24 July 2022 (Attachment 150d)
19-21 Aug 2022 (Attachment 150e)
16-18 Sept 2022 (Attachment 150f)
21-23 Oct 2022 (Attachment 150g)
4-6 Nov 2022 (Attachment 150h)
Based on the 1st – 7th verifications process, there were 324 beneficiaries or the Solar PV Rooftop Incentive applicants who passed the verification process, with a total estimated incentive value of IDR 7,963,750,000.
1st Verification : 15 beneficiaries, with a total incentive value of IDR 115,400,000
2nd Verification : 13 beneficiaries, with a total incentive value of IDR 139,350,000
3rd Verification : 33 beneficiaries, with a total incentive value of IDR 249,000,000
4th Verification : 44 beneficiaries, with a total incentive value of IDR 1,566,350,000
5th Verification : 82 beneficiaries, with a total incentive value of IDR 1,996,600,000
6th Verification : 38 beneficiaries, with a total incentive value of IDR 1,295,950,000
7th Verification : 99 beneficiaries, with a total incentive value of IDR 2,601,100,000
For the 8th Verification, there are 60 potential beneficiaries who can process further for the 9th Verification (on 9 December 2022) and payment process, with a total estimated incentive value of IDR 15,415,322,794 (as of 15 Nov 2022).
In order to widening the opportunity for public in getting the Solar PV Rooftop Incentive, as well as encouraging the public investment in Solar PV Rooftop, UNDP and DJEBTKE ESDM has updated the ‘SEF Grant Incentive for Solar PV Rooftop’ terms & condition and required performance criteria. (Attachment 151a,b)
2.3.1 Facilitation and Technical Assistance to selected RE projects in the Financial Close (FC) and Issuance of Power Purchasing Agreement (PPA) of SEF-assisted projects with PLN
MTRE3 project has been facilitating the ‘study on the indigenous people assessment and chance find procedure’ at Mini Hydro Power Plant (PLTM) Maiting Hulu-2 (8MW), in order to fulfill the corrective action plan (CAP) from PT. SMI. The study aims to identify the potential impact of the PLTM Maiting Hulu-2 project on indigenous people in Maiting Hulu, North Toraja. In addition, the study will provide recommendations on the future mitigation measures through relevant programs regarding socio-cultural aspects around the PLTM project site. The kick off meeting for the study was conducted on 11 March 2022 (Attachment 152), while the site visit process was carried out during 18-22 April 2022. The report of the study has been finalized and submitted in October 2022 (Attachment 165a,b).
In order to leverage the household’s access to RE based electricity, MTRE3 plans to facilitate additional RE projects with total potential capacity more than 5MW.
In addition, several studies have been developing on the SEF Batch-1 facilitation to 11 Renewable Energy/Energy Efficiency (RE/EE) projects:
1. Biomass Power Plant PLTBm Kundur – 2.4MW
2. Biomass Power Plant (PLTBm) Ujung Batu – 5MW
3. Hydro Power Plant (PLTA) Luteung – 16MW
4. Hydro Power Plant (PLTA) Sangir – 19MW
5. Mini Hydro Power Plant (PLTM) Pareang – 2.8MW
6. Mini Hydro Power Plant (PLTM) Cisomang – 4MW
7. Mini Hydro Power Plant (PLTM) Cimandiri - 4.4 MW
8. Mini Hydro Power Plant (PLTM) Padang Guci-2 – 7MW
9. Mini Hydro Power Plant (PLTM) Maiting Hulu-2 - 8MW
10. Green building Certification at Banyuwangi Airport
11. ESCO implementation at Graha Niaga Building
The purpose of the study is to find alternative approaches to funding the implementation of SEF Facility.
Besides, MTRE3 also gives a facilitation outside the SEF to the private sector (PT Sido Muncul) through Energy Management System (EMS) Technical Assistance (Attachment 166). This facilitation aims to conduct Energy Management System Mapping for selected holding companies and map out the potential annual energy saving, GHG emission reduction calculation and report, as well as sustainable energy investments.
3.1.1 Verification of RE and EE Pilot Projects by Accredited Institutional Third Party GHG Verifier
On-going validation is conducted by third party verification for 6 (six) MTRE3’s pilot project:
1. Mini-hydro Power Plant (6 MW Padang Guci 1 Run-off River)
2. Solar PV Power Plant (5 MWp Kupang)
3. Biomass Power Plant (1 MW Tanjung Batu Woodchips Gasification)
4. Biogas Power Plant (2.4 MW POME Waste Treatment)
5. Energy Efficiency in Buildings at Gedung Slamet Bratanata
6. Energy Efficiency in Buildings at Menara Ravindo
Application form submitted to validation & verification body/institution in March 2022. The analyzing of Project Design Document is ongoing by the V/V institution. (Attachment 153a-f)
Guidelines of Monitoring Reporting Verification (MRV) for each type of RE power plant & EE building are developed. MTRE3 also developed a book of methodology on emission calculation and published by the Ministry of Environment and Forestry as a focal point on emission reduction in Indonesia. (Attachment 154)
3.2.1 Advocate Policy for ICER
The MTRE3 Project facilitates the derived rule of Presidential Regulation number 98/2021. Regulation needed are:
1. Minister of Environment and Forestry Regulation on Governance of Carbon Trading
2. Minister of Energy Regulation on Governance of Carbon Pricing on Power Sector
Both drafts are available through the facilitation process of MTRE3 from Q4 of 2021. Period of January - October 2022, the process continued with:
1. Stakeholder consultation in Power Sector attended by representative from PLN (State Electricity Company) & IPP (Independent Power Producer)
2. Series of meeting with several line minister (include: Coordinating Ministry of Maritime and Investment, Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Environment and Forestry, Ministry of Law, UNDP Expert)
n order to support the implementation of MRV process for mitigation actions that is integrated with the carbon trading system, MTRE3 Project has been facilitating the integration between the power plant mitigation action registration at ‘APPLE Gatrik’ system from MEMR/ESDM and the carbon registry at ‘SRN’ system from MoEF/KLHK through the facilitation of a series of FGDs. The Minister of Environment & Forestry stipulates Ministerial Regulation number 21 of 2022 on September 21st concerning Procedures for Implementing Carbon Economic Values / NEK.
3.3.1 Develop Competency Standard for Individual Third Party GHG Verifier
This activity will contribute to the development of standard method and guideline for implementation of MRV for pilot projects on RE-based power generation and energy efficiency in commercial building sectors, which will be implemented by individual verifier. Currently, the verification process is conducted by institutions with high cost for small scale mitigation action. During February to March 2022, MTRE3 Project has conducted training and socialization about the data input mitigation action for isolated grid to related stakeholders.
? Training for trainer to DJK-ESDM staff for input data mitigation action (16 February 2022), virtual by zoom
? Training & socialization data input for power plant manager/staff (22-23 February - on grid) (150 participants from 145 power plants), virtual by zoom
In addition, MTRE3 Project facilitated a meeting for the coal power plant management unit to input the inventory data which was used by the government to set emission caps for year 2022 (using data year 2021) on 28-30 March 2022.

Marginal Abatement Cost Curve (MACC) report for 4 pilot provinces has been completed as Pre-final draft in the end of June 2020. MACC report for 4 provinces will be finalized in the mid of August 2020, when the report receives official buy-in from National and Provincial Government.
The outcome 2 has progressed on the activity on going for the operation “Integrated Market Service Center” (IMSC) to support sustainable RE & EE investments. The function of intended IMSC in each province will be added to the existing regional permitting and investment agency, Dinas Penanaman Modal dan Perijinan Terpadu Satu Pintu (DPMPTSP). In 2020, 9 (nine) small-to-medium scale RE/EE projects that were financially supported by the Sustainable Energy Fund, a total of USD 896,245 from SEF budget has been used to support 9 projects under the SEF facility and 4 (four) Climate Mitigation Concept Notes has been served as baseline to develop more elaborated version of 4 Climate Mitigation Proposal in energy sector by November 2020. In addition, the 0.22 MW of RE investment project was also being implemented, and in total of 52,886.68 m2 has energy efficient.
For the target of Outcome 3, 7 (seven) registered mitigation actions in energy sector that were endorsed by the MEMR and MoEF. In 2020, there was 1 (one) MRV report submitted to MoEF ,following nationally agreed standard method and guidance.
